title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Client Tunnel Verification
verification_method: Focused HTTP/3 WebSocket loopback tests, adjacent RFC 9220 regression tests, SpecTrace JSON validation, generated coverage triage, and diff hygiene.
scope: This verification covers a local HTTP/3 client opening an RFC 9220 WebSocket Extended CONNECT tunnel to the repository server over QUIC loopback, writing a masked binary client message, receiving an unmasked server echo, and refusing to open the helper when local `SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL` was not advertised.
preconditions: Server-side WebSocket tunnel dispatch remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0003`.
Endpoint-role-aware WebSocket frame parsing remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0002`.
expected_result: The focused client tunnel tests pass, the adjacent WebSocket regression filter passes, the new RFC 9220 client tunnel requirement is trace-clean, SpecTrace validation accepts the artifacts, and diff hygiene is clean.
status_summary: The HTTP/3 client can now open a locally verified RFC 9220 WebSocket Extended CONNECT tunnel and exchange WebSocket messages with the local server. Evidence class is local same-process HTTP/3 QUIC loopback; it is not external peer interoperability, published ProtocolLab evidence, or isolated-host proof.
